harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Distributed MinIO is operational across node1–node4 with authenticated TLS S3 access on port 9000. Bucket infra-data contains proof.txt with the exact required content. One-member outage operations, rejoin/healing, and sequential restart persistence were verified.
actions_performed: Configured four MinIO members on the dedicated 10.100.206.0/24 network.
Generated credentials and TLS certificates on-node without exposing secrets.
Configured MinIO Client administration on node1.
Verified reads and writes with node4 unavailable, then verified its rejoin and healed local shard.
Restarted every node individually and verified changed boot identities, mounted storage, MinIO recovery, cluster health, and persisted objects.

evidence.requirement: Authenticated TLS S3 service and four-member cluster
evidence.summary: TLS verification succeeds, every health endpoint returns 200, and MinIO reports 4/4 network connectivity with four online drives and EC:2.

evidence.requirement: Bucket infra-data and exact proof.txt content
evidence.summary: Authenticated mc operations created the bucket, uploaded the object, and returned distributed-storage-ready before and after restarts.

evidence.requirement: Readable and writable during one-member outage
evidence.summary: node4 is proven inactive while proof.txt remains readable and a new object is successfully written and read with 3/4 members.
node4 automatically rejoins at 4/4, serves the outage-written object, and its missing shard heals from Yellow to Green.
Healthy baseline and boot ID were captured, restart acknowledged, boot ID changed, storage remounted, MinIO recovered, and both objects remained readable.
Healthy baseline and boot ID were captured, restart acknowledged, boot ID changed, MinIO and persistent data recovered with cluster health 200.
Baseline, sequential restart acknowledgements, changed boot identities, mounted data, active MinIO, local objects, and health 200 were captured.
Healthy baseline and boot ID were captured, restart acknowledged, boot ID changed, MinIO and both local object shards recovered with health 200.

attempts.error: The Antrieb managed cluster lease expired

diagnosis.summary: Attempt 1 did not configure or verify MinIO. Every recorded node command was rejected before execution because the managed-cluster lease had expired. There is no evidence of any MinIO, TLS, bucket, object, failover, recovery, or persistence state, so configuration defects cannot be assessed.

evidence.finding: All five terminal records have outcome `cluster_expired`; four baseline checks targeted node1–node4 and one minimal retry targeted node1.
Each execution failed with MCP error -32000: “The Antrieb managed cluster lease expired.” No command IDs or node output were returned.
The executor explicitly reported that no configuration, verification, degraded-member test, or restart protocol could be performed.

No successful command or structured executor report exists. The evidence is therefore insufficient to infer whether networking, storage, certificates, credentials, or MinIO configuration would have worked.

likely_causes.cause: The immediate failure was expiration of the managed-cluster lease before the recorded node operations could execute.

The session likely consumed too much of its lease before beginning actionable node work; the available timestamps and large interaction footprint suggest delay, but do not establish what consumed the time.
Any MinIO-specific failure is unsupported: no MinIO command reached a node.

next_attempt_guidance: Begin node inspection and implementation immediately after provisioning; keep commands small and track remaining lease time.
On every node, identify the dedicated-storage NIC and its IPv4 address with `ip -br -4 addr` and verify peer routing with `ip route get`. Do not guess interface names or addresses.
Give all four storage endpoints stable names resolving to their dedicated-network addresses. Verify node1 can reach ports 9000/9001 on every peer before service testing.

Prepare one data path per node, install the same MinIO release everywhere, and configure identical root credentials plus TLS certificates whose SANs cover every hostname/IP clients and peers will use.
Create a systemd service on all nodes using the same four dedicated-network endpoints, such as `https://node{1...4}:9000/<data-path>`, and enable automatic restart/startup.
Install `mc` on node1, configure an authenticated HTTPS alias, create `infra-data`, upload `proof.txt` containing exactly `distributed-storage-ready`, and verify its contents.
Prove tolerance explicitly: stop MinIO on one storage node; from node1, read the original object and write/read a new object while that node is absent.

Restart the stopped member, confirm it rejoins through `mc admin info`, allow automatic healing, and verify the object written during the outage is readable through the restored member. Capture service status and relevant logs.
Finish with a restart/persistence check while lease time remains, recording command output for TLS access, bucket/object contents, degraded reads and writes, rejoin, and healed data.

attempts.summary: Distributed MinIO is operational across node1–node4 with authenticated TLS S3 access on port 9000. Bucket infra-data contains proof.txt with the exact required content. One-member outage operations, rejoin/healing, and sequential restart persistence were verified.
